About Our Farm

We’re dedicated to ethically raising grass-finished beef and outdoor-living chickens, all while staying true to humane and sustainable practices that respect both the animals and the land.

Meet Kyle, the guy behind Clover Farms

Meet Kyle, the guy behind Clover Farms. His best days are hanging out with the cows and roaming with the chickens.

Kyle’s journey from New Jersey to farming in Jacksonville is all about returning to his roots and following his passion. Growing up, he spent countless hours at his best friend’s family beef farm, while his grandfather ran Skinner's Dairy, one of Jacksonville’s largest dairy operations. Though born in Jacksonville, he moved away at age five but came back after high school. In his early 20s, he worked on a dairy farm before spending more than a decade in corporate America.

When the chance to start farming came along in his 30's, he jumped at it and launched Clover Farms, diving back into what he loves. Always health-conscious, Kyle was determined to create a farm that not only produced nutrient-dense meat in a humane way, but also enriched the soil for future generations.

CONTACT KYLE
Clover Farm's Values

Our Heart

At Clover Farms, we’re more than just a farm—we’re a community deeply rooted in Northeast Florida, caring for over 1,000 beating hearts out here in the fields.  Our premium beef and eggs comes from our own farm, as well as a like-minded local partners within Florida and Georgia. We’re dedicated to ethically raising grass-finished beef and outdoor-living chickens, all while staying true to humane and sustainable practices that respect both the animals and the land.

Our Land

Our vision extends far beyond the pasture. Kyle’s passion for farming drives us to embrace regenerative techniques that not only cultivate the land but nurture it and boost soil health. By rotating our cattle across different pastures and keeping the ground well-covered, we help the soil stay rich and full of life. Our cows contribute naturally, as their grazing stirs the earth and their manure adds valuable nutrients. This process restores the land, supports biodiversity, and strengthens the environment for future generations.

Our Promise

It's simple: we will never grow for today at the expense of tomorrow. We’re not just growing food—we’re starting a movement. Our mission is to provide you with locally grown, wholesome, and sustainable foods that nourish both your family and the environment. We sincerely hope you’ll join us on this journey toward a more sustainable future.

Grass-Fed Beef Delivery Across Florida and Georgia

Clover Farms is a family farm in Northeast Florida raising USDA-inspected, 100% grass-fed, grass-finished beef and pasture-raised eggs. If you live in Florida or South Georgia, we can get real food to you.

Areas We Serve

For some of you, we hand it to you in person at local farmers' markets. Some of you get it packed and dropped at your door. Either way, it comes from the same herd, raised the same way, on open pasture.

Here is where we deliver, where you can meet us in person, and what is coming next.

Grass-Fed Beef Delivery by City

We ship across Florida and Georgia. These pages cover what delivery looks like in each city, which cuts people there order most, and how to get started.

Jacksonville Grass-Fed Beef: our home city, with local pickup and three weekly markets
Orlando Grass-Fed Beef: shipped to your door across Central Florida
Tampa Grass-Fed Beef: shipped to homes and restaurants on the Gulf side
Miami Grass-Fed Beef: shipped to South Florida, hard-frozen and packed with ice
Coming Soon

We are building out pages for more of the state. St. Augustine, Gainesville, Daytona Beach, Ocala, Sarasota, Naples, and Fort Myers are next up. You do not have to wait for a page to order, though. If you are anywhere in Florida or Georgia, we already ship to you.

Local Pickup Around Jacksonville

If you are close to home, you can skip shipping altogether and pick up your order. It is cheaper, it is fresher, and you get to say hello.

Farmers Markets
Atlantic Beach Farmers Market. Jack Russell Park, 800 Seminole Rd, Jacksonville. Sundays, 10 am to 2 pm.
Murray Hill Farmers Market. Fishweir Brewing Company, 1183 Edgewood Ave S, Jacksonville. Wednesdays, 5 pm to 8 pm.
St. Augustine Amphitheater Farmers Market. 1340C A1A S, St. Augustine. Saturdays, 8:30 am to 12:30 pm.

Full details on the farmers markets page.

Weekly Pickup Spots

We also run Monday afternoon pickups at the Beaches, Riverside, and San Marco, plus by-appointment pickup for beef shares. Times and addresses are on the pick up locations page.

Local Stores

A few shops around town carry our products year-round. See the current list on the local stores page.

What We Ship, and Where

We ship to Florida and Georgia only. Orders go out weekly, packed hard-frozen with ice so everything arrives solid. Beef, tallow, and body care all ship. Eggs do not, since fresh eggs and a cardboard box in a Florida summer do not mix. Eggs are pickup only, at markets and our local spots.

The shipping page has current rates and the weekly cutoff. If you are new here, how it works walks through ordering start to finish.

Common Questions
Do you ship outside Florida and Georgia?

Not right now. Keeping the shipping radius tight is how we get beef to you hard-frozen instead of half-thawed. If you are outside FL and GA and want to be told when that changes, join our email list at the bottom of any page.

Do I have to live in one of the cities listed to order?

No. The city pages are there because those are the places we hear from most, but we ship anywhere in Florida and Georgia. Small towns included.

Can I pick up if I do not live in Jacksonville?

Plenty of people drive in from St. Augustine, Ponte Vedra, and Nocatee to catch us at a market. If you are within an hour or so, pickup is usually worth it. Beyond that, shipping is easier on everybody.

Where does the beef actually come from?

Our own herd here in Northeast Florida, plus a handful of like-minded family farms in Florida and Georgia that raise cattle the way we do. No feedlots, no grain finishing, no hormones, no antibiotics. Ever.

Ready to Order?

Start with the beef, stock the freezer with a beef share, or grab a dozen pasture-raised eggs at the next market.

Buying a Beef Share: Whole, Half, or Quarter?
FEBRUARY 22, 2026
Share

Buying a grass-fed, grass-finished beef share is one of the smartest ways to fill your freezer with high-quality beef while supporting a local farm you trust. If you’ve been curious about how it works or which option makes the most sense for your family, this guide will walk you through it.

Table of Contents
What Is a Beef Share?
How the Process Works: From Farm to Freezer
Whole vs. Half vs. Quarter: What’s in Each Share?
Why the Half Share Is Our Most Popular Option
How Much Freezer Space You’ll Need
Is a Beef Share Worth it?
Why We Love Beef Shares at Clover Farms

 

What is a Beef Share?

A grass-fed, grass-finished beef share means you are purchasing a portion of a whole animal rather than individual cuts one package at a time. Instead of shopping steak by steak, you receive a variety of cuts all at once, including premium steaks, roasts, ground beef, and more.

It’s a return to the traditional way families sourced meat for generations. You stock up, eat seasonally, and know exactly where your beef comes from.

 

How the Process Works: From Farm to Freezer

When you reserve a beef share, you are securing your portion of a 100 percent grass-fed, grass-finished animal raised right here on pasture. Once processed, your share is cut, vacuum-sealed, clearly labeled, and immediately frozen to ensure freshness for your freezer.

The process generally takes 30-45 days from the time you order to the time we ship. We’ll communicate timing, pickup details, and what to expect every step of the way. It’s simple, transparent, and worth the planning.

 

Whole vs. Half vs. Quarter: What's in Each Share?

The biggest difference between share sizes is quantity, freezer space, and overall savings per pound.

Below is a simple comparison table. Please note, the number and size of cuts can vary from bundle to bundle as no two cows are exactly alike. 

Cut / Item	Whole	Half	Quarter
Ribeye Steaks	20	10	5
New York Strip Steaks	20	10	5
Filet Mignon Steaks	10	5	2
Top Sirloin Steaks (Baseball Cut)	16	8	4
Outside Skirt Steaks	4	2	0
Flat Iron Steaks	4	2	1
Flank Steaks	4	2	1
Fajita Skirt Steaks	12	6	3
Stew Meat	24	12	6
Chuck Roast Boneless	8	4	1
Top Round	4	2	2
Coulotte	2	1	0
Tri-Tip Roast	2	1	0
Eye of Round	2	1	0
Rump Roast	6	3	1
Short Ribs Bone-In	2	1	0
Brisket Deckle Off	2	1	0
Ground Beef (80/20)	300	150	75

 

 

Why the Half Share is Our Most Popular Option

If you’re unsure which route to take, the half share is the sweet spot for most families. It offers a strong balance of variety, value, and manageable freezer space. You get a generous selection of premium steaks and roasts, plenty of ground beef for everyday meals, and a better price per pound compared to buying individual cuts.

For many households, a half share provides months of high-quality beef without overwhelming your freezer. It’s the option we recommend most often because it makes the biggest impact without requiring the commitment of a whole animal.

 

How Much Freezer Space Will You Need

Freezer space is one of the most common questions we get.

As a general guideline:

Whole share: typically requires a dedicated chest freezer. Approximately 490lbs and need about 13 cubic feet of freezer space to store.
Half share: Approximately 245 lbs. & 6.5 cubic feet of freezer space is needed for this beef share.
Quarter share: can often fit in the freezer section of a refrigerator plus a small chest freezer.  Approximately 110 lbs. & 3 cubic feet of freezer space is needed for this beef share.

Planning ahead ensures your beef is stored properly and stays organized.

Is a Beef Share Worth It?

For families who value clean, grass-fed beef and want to simplify grocery shopping, the answer is usually yes. You lock in your supply of grass-fed, grass-finished beef, reduce store trips, and enjoy better value per pound. Most importantly, you know exactly how your food was raised.

If you’ve been thinking about filling your freezer, now is a great time to reserve your share. And if you’re new to the process, start with the half share. It’s our most popular option for a reason.

Why We Love Beef Shares at Clover Farms

Beef shares aren’t just a bulk purchase. They’re a partnership. Your investment supports regenerative practices that build healthy soil, raise animals the right way, and strengthen our land for the long haul.

When you purchase a whole, half, or quarter share, you help us honor the entire animal, reduce waste, and keep pricing sustainable for families who care about real food.
